beats_top.query: cornell international student jobs on campus F-1 how to find
beats_top.why: The #1 result is Cornell's official rules page, which gives limits but not the ordered path (Workday search, I-9 timing, SSN sequencing, taxes). Our first paragraph answers the question and the steps fill that gap.
changes: Fix the unsupported 'not placed, not guaranteed' attribution so every claim is traceable.
Name Form 8843 in the tax section and say how the I-9 is actually done (Workday notice, then original documents shown to a Cornell representative).

fixes: In step 3, remove the sentence 'Student Employment says students are not placed in jobs, and jobs are not guaranteed' with its link to https://studentemployment.cornell.edu/find-a-job (that page does not say it), or replace it with a link to an official Cornell page that does say it. Do not attribute it to the Find a Job page.

In the hours table and 'Common mistakes', either remove 'total across all campus jobs' and 'combined total' or present it as our reading of the 20-hour maximum rather than a Cornell statement; https://international.globallearning.cornell.edu/node/182 says only that exactly 20 hours is the weekly maximum.

In step 4, replace 'Student workers can submit the form through Workday' with wording the sources support: after hiring you get a Workday notification to complete Form I-9, then present original documents to an authorized Cornell representative (https://studentemployment.cornell.edu/resources/i-9-form); link the HR guide for students completing the I-9 in Workday (https://hr.cornell.edu/browse-self-service/workday-help-student-workers).

In the Taxes section, name the form you must send the IRS even with no U.S. income as Form 8843 (source https://international.globallearning.cornell.edu/employment-and-taxes/us-income-tax-basics) and note that you generally do not file a return in that case.
